stepTexts.heat_pan: Warm a cast-iron or heavy skillet over medium heat and melt the butter.
stepTexts.crisp_bacon: Lay in the bacon and cook until the edges are browned and crisp while the centre stays tender.
stepTexts.add_eggs: Move the bacon toward the sides of the pan, then crack the eggs into the open centre without breaking the yolks.
stepTexts.finish_eggs: Lower the heat and cook gently until the whites are set and the yolks are still soft.
stepTexts.season_serve: Finish with black pepper and serve immediately with toasted rustic bread.

miso_paste.name: Miso paste
miso_paste.note: soy sauce can be used for a lighter alternative

stepTexts.season_broth: Heat the broth gently and whisk in the miso until smooth. Keep it hot without letting it reduce aggressively.
stepTexts.cook_noodles: Cook the ramen noodles separately according to their package timing, then drain thoroughly.
stepTexts.fill_bowls: Divide the hot noodles between two bowls and ladle over enough broth to surround them.
stepTexts.add_toppings: Arrange the chashu, halved marinated eggs, narutomaki, spring onion, bean sprouts and nori over the noodles.
stepTexts.serve: Serve immediately while the broth and noodles are piping hot.

stepTexts.simmer_onion: Combine dashi, soy sauce, mirin and sugar in a small skillet. Add the onion and simmer until softened.
stepTexts.add_tonkatsu: Slice the fried pork cutlets into strips and lay them over the seasoned onion.
stepTexts.add_eggs: Beat the eggs only lightly, then pour them over the cutlets so distinct streaks of white and yolk remain.
stepTexts.steam_finish: Cover and cook briefly, stopping while the egg is still soft and creamy rather than fully firm.
stepTexts.assemble_bowl: Fill two bowls with hot rice, slide the pork-and-egg mixture on top and finish with peas or chives.

anko.name: Sweet red-bean paste (anko)
anko.note: hazelnut spread can be used as an alternative

stepTexts.whisk_base: Whisk the eggs with the sugar and honey until the mixture looks lighter and slightly foamy.
stepTexts.finish_batter: Mix the baking powder into the water, add it to the bowl and fold in the sifted flour until the batter is smooth.
stepTexts.rest_batter: Chill the batter for 15 minutes so it can settle before cooking.
stepTexts.cook_first_side: Heat a non-stick pan over low heat, wipe it with a very thin film of oil and spoon in small rounds of batter. Cook until bubbles appear on top.
stepTexts.cook_second_side: Turn each round and cook the second side briefly until evenly coloured.
stepTexts.fill_dorayaki: Let the cakes cool, then sandwich them in pairs with anko in the centre and gently press the edges into the classic rounded shape.

salt.name: Salt
salt.note: a small pinch plus a little for shaping

stepTexts.wash_cook_rice: Rinse the rice several times until the water runs much clearer. Cook it with the measured water, covered, over low heat.
stepTexts.rest_rice: Turn off the heat and leave the rice covered for 10 minutes before shaping.
stepTexts.make_filling: Mix the drained tuna with the Japanese mayonnaise and a small pinch of salt.
stepTexts.fill_shape: Moisten and lightly salt your hands. Flatten a portion of warm rice, add a little tuna filling in the centre, cover with more rice and shape into a compact triangle.
stepTexts.finish_nori: Wrap a strip of nori around the base. Add sesame or furikake if desired and serve while the rice is still pleasantly warm.

okonomiyaki_sauce.name: Okonomiyaki sauce
okonomiyaki_sauce.note: or a mixture of ketchup, Worcestershire sauce and honey

aoki_seaweed.name: Aoki seaweed
aoki_seaweed.note: as named in the source reference

stepTexts.make_batter: Whisk the flour, cold dashi and egg until the batter is smooth and evenly combined.
stepTexts.add_cabbage: Fold in the finely sliced cabbage until it is well coated by the batter.
stepTexts.shape_and_top: Heat a lightly oiled griddle or skillet, spoon in the mixture as a thick round and lay the pork slices across the top.
stepTexts.cook_both_sides: Cook covered over medium heat until the first side is set, then turn carefully and continue until the pork side is browned and the centre is cooked through.
stepTexts.finish: Transfer to a plate and finish with okonomiyaki sauce, Japanese mayonnaise, katsuobushi and the seaweed garnish.

stepTexts.make_batter: Whisk the flour, egg and cold dashi into a thin, smooth batter.
stepTexts.heat_pan: Heat a takoyaki pan thoroughly and oil each cavity well.
stepTexts.fill_moulds: Pour batter into the cavities almost to the top.
stepTexts.add_fillings: Add a piece of octopus to each cavity together with a little pickled ginger, tenkasu and spring onion.
stepTexts.turn_balls: As the bottoms set, use wooden picks to rotate the pieces gradually, tucking in loose batter until rounded and evenly browned.
stepTexts.finish: Serve hot with takoyaki sauce, Japanese mayonnaise and katsuobushi.

stepTexts.cook_rice_filling: Sauté the chicken and onion in a lightly oiled pan. Add the steamed rice and ketchup, then toss until the rice is evenly coated and hot.
stepTexts.shape_rice: Shape the seasoned rice into a neat oval mound on a plate.
stepTexts.beat_eggs: Beat the eggs with the milk and a little salt and pepper.
stepTexts.cook_omelette: Melt the butter in a clean pan over medium-low heat and cook the eggs as a soft, flexible omelette.
stepTexts.wrap_and_decorate: Lay the omelette over the rice so it covers the mound, then decorate the top with a heart or short message in ketchup.

stepTexts.season_broth: Bring the dashi, soy sauce, mirin and sugar to a gentle boil in a small skillet.
stepTexts.cook_chicken: Add the onion and chicken, cover and cook over medium heat until the chicken is cooked through and the onion has softened.
stepTexts.first_egg: Beat the eggs lightly and pour roughly three quarters over the chicken. Cover and cook briefly so the egg begins to set.
stepTexts.finish_egg: Add the remaining egg, turn off the heat and cover for a short rest so the surface stays soft and creamy.
stepTexts.assemble: Spoon the chicken, egg and seasoned broth over bowls of hot rice and finish with mitsuba or chives.

pumpkin.name: Pumpkin
pumpkin.note: Delica or Mantovana type, cleaned and cubed

stepTexts.cook_pumpkin: Cook the pumpkin until tender, mash it into a coarse purée and season with salt, pepper and nutmeg.
stepTexts.cook_fish: Soften the chopped onion in a pan with a little oil, add the fish and cook briefly so the flavours combine.
stepTexts.assemble_filling: Spread the pumpkin over the base of a baking dish, add the fish and onion, scatter over the sliced black olives and cover with béchamel.
stepTexts.cover_and_decorate: Lay the puff pastry over the dish. Use any trimmings to make a simple fish-shaped decoration for the top.
stepTexts.bake: Brush the pastry with egg yolk and bake in a preheated 200°C static oven until the pastry is deeply golden.
